main_text.p: synecdochen. Sic Prouerb.25.21. Roman.12.20. Inde sunt phrases Hebraeis familiares: Panem edere, pro cibum capere, Marc.3.20. & 7.2. panem frangere, ibidem pro capere cibum, Act.2.46. panis fractio, pro mutuo conuictu & conuiuiis, quae inter Iudaeos celebrantur, 2, 42. (Vide FRACTIO.) panis item capitur pro eo cibi genere, quod panem vocamus, Marc.8.4. panis hominem fulcit, Genes.3.19. Eccles.11,6. Ephes.4.28. 1 Thessal.4.11. 2 Thessal.3.10. Tit.3.14. panes facierum (quos Latine propositionis, vel propositivos vertunt) Hebraeis ideo sic dicuntur, Exod.25.30. Leuit.24 v.5.7. Matth.12.4. Marc 2.26. Luc.6.4. Heb.9.2. quod coram Domino appositi tota hebdomade manerent in aurea mensa, huic cultui consecrata, sicut edixit Dominus Leuitic.24.5. appositivos non inepte vocaueris. Panes multiplicantur, (Vide MIRACVLA) panis Evangelij, Iudaeorum erat, Matt.15.26 &c. Marc.7.27. panis laicus, vt vocant, 1 Sam.21.4. panis vitae, hoc est, panis vivificus, (Hebraismus) caro Christi, Ioann.6.v.35.51. panis vnius & calicis participatio, 1 Corinth.10.16. panes primitiarum multiplicati, 2 Regum 4.42. pane & aqua cibatur Elias, 1 Reg.19.v.6.8. pane solo non viuit homo, Deut.8.3. Matt.4.4. Luc.4.4. panibus obedientium sibi benedixit Deus, comeduntq; in saturitate, Leu.26.5. panes pluit Deus e coelo, Exo.16.13. panibus quinque, quinque hominum millia saturati. Matt.14.v.17.21. septem, quatuor millia 15.v.34.38. panum oblatio, Leu.2.4.

1. Frequenter quemuis cibum, vel tenuem, vel lautum significat: vt ex contextuum circumstantiis apparet. Quando autem cum adiecto legitur (vt Gen.18.6. Exo.12. v.8 39. & alibi panem purum vt plurimum significat.
2. Panis afflictionis, oppressionis, tribulationis, lacrymarum, Deut.16.3. 1 Reg.22.27. Psal. 42.4. & 80.6. & 127. Esai. 30.20.
3. Panis impietatis & mendacij, i. pessimis artibus comparatus, Prou.4.17. & 23.3.
5. Panes propositionis, seu facierum, qui coram facie Dei i. mensa in tabernaculo, apponebantur, Exo.25.30. Num 4.7. 1 Sam.21.v.4.6. Matt.12.4. Heb.9.2.

page.notes: The right margin holds faint, very small notes that are cut off by the facing page; they cannot be read and are not transcribed. The word "vocula" is doubtful. The bracket before "PANIS" is printed. The text ends on "6. Pani" at the right edge, where the line is cut off.
